chunks: From him, from Abu Ishaq, from Ali ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Lending a thousand dirhams twice is more beloved to me than giving it in charity once. And just as it is not permissible for your debtor to delay you when he is wealthy, so too it is not permissible for you to delay him when you know that he is insolvent.'

key_terms.أُقْرِضُهَا: I lend it (verb form indicating lending)
key_terms.تُعْسِرَهُ: You delay him (from the root of insolvency/poverty)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on delaying a debtor or creditor based on their financial status?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), elevates the act of lending (iqrad) above single-instance charity (sadaqah) by emphasizing the sustained relational bond and mercy it fosters. It establishes a reciprocal legal principle where financial capacity dictates the duty of leniency: a wealthy creditor must not delay a poor debtor, just as a poor debtor must not delay a wealthy creditor, ensuring equity in debt management. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'ihsan' (excellence) in financial dealings, moving beyond mere contractual obligation to moral consideration of the debtor's actual ability to pay.
